findings.title: Backup code alone can authenticate without the account password
findings.body: The password is only verified by the block at lines 121-129, which is guarded by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new backup-code branch is entered whenever `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is set, regardless of `totpCode`. An attacker who obtains a single backup code (e.g. the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt`) but does not know the password can POST to the credentials endpoint with `email`, an arbitrary `password`, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") and the valid `backupCode`: the password check is skipped because `totpCode` is truthy, and only the backup code is validated, so the login succeeds. Backup codes are intended to replace the second factor, not the password, so this turns them into full single-factor credentials. The backup-code branch must verify the password (or the branch selection must not depend on `totpCode` being absent).

findings.title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hashed
findings.body: Backup codes are persisted as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, i.e. recoverable plaintext. The server never needs to display the codes again after setup (they are only shown from the setup response), so they can and should be stored as one-way hashes like passwords. As implemented, anyone who gains read access to the users table together with the (single, global, long-lived) encryption key — which is also present in every app instance's environment — can recover every user's 2FA backup codes and bypass two-factor auth for all accounts.

findings.title: onEnable() is no longer called unless the user clicks "Close", leaving stale UI after enabling 2FA
findings.body: Previously `onEnable()` was invoked as soon as the enable request succeeded. Now it is only called by the "Close" button on the backup-codes step. If the user dismisses the dialog with the X / overlay / Esc (which goes through `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent is never notified, so the settings page never invalidates its query and the two-factor switch keeps showing "off" until a manual reload. Additionally `resetState()` is not run on that path, so `step` stays at `DisplayBackupCodes` and re-opening the modal shows the previous (now stale) backup codes screen instead of the password step. Either call `onEnable()` when the enable request succeeds, or handle `onOpenChange` to invoke `onEnable()`/`resetState()`.

findings.title: First 2FA test asserts nothing and is not updated for the new backup-codes step
findings.body: `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the returned Promise, which is always truthy, so the step verifies nothing — the PR documents this with a FIXME instead of fixing it. This matters now: with the new flow the backup-codes dialog stays open after OTP entry and `onEnable()` is never fired, so the switch would legitimately not be checked; the test only passes because the assertion is a no-op. Use `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` after dismissing the backup-codes dialog, as the second test does.

findings.title: "missing_backup_codes" message points users to a settings feature that does not exist
findings.body: The string is "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but there is no UI anywhere in this PR to generate or regenerate backup codes — codes are only created inside the 2FA setup flow (`totp/setup`). Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration has `backupCodes = null` and will hit this message with no actionable path; the only way to obtain codes is to disable and re-enable 2FA. Either add a regenerate action or change the message to tell users to disable and re-enable two-factor authentication.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive while the input is not normalized
findings.body: `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` compares the user input literally against lowercase hex codes generated by `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`. The input field in `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx` sets no `autoCapitalize="off"`/`autoCorrect="off"`, so mobile keyboards commonly capitalize the first character and users who type the code in upper case will be rejected with "Backup code is incorrect" even though they supplied a valid code. The same applies to `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`. Normalize with `.toLowerCase().trim()` server-side and/or disable auto-capitalization on the input.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code decrypts the whole array, nulls one entry and writes the re-encrypted blob back with a plain `user.update`. Two concurrent logins using the same backup code both read the un-consumed array and both succeed, so a one-time code can be used more than once; two concurrent logins using different codes will clobber each other's update, resurrecting an already-used code. Consider a transaction with a row-level check (e.g. conditional update on the previous value) or storing individual code rows that can be deleted atomically.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code silently does nothing
findings.body: The login form is rendered with `noValidate`, and the zod schema only validates `email`/`password` (`.passthrough()`), so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the backup-code input are not enforced. Submitting the backup-code screen with an empty field sends `backupCode: ""`, the server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` — a no-op since the user is already on that screen — while `errorMessage` was cleared at the start of submit. The user gets no feedback at all. Validate the backup code client-side or surface an error for this case.

findings.title: Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string; a client sending `{"backupCode": 123}` or an object causes an uncaught `TypeError` and an opaque 500 instead of a 400. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on line 58 is unguarded, so a corrupted/re-keyed `backupCodes` column throws an unhandled exception rather than returning a meaningful error. Validate/parse the body (e.g. with zod) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch.

findings.title: Backup code state and object URL are never cleaned up
findings.body: `resetState()` only clears password, error and step; `backupCodes` and `backupCodesUrl` keep holding the generated codes in component state after the dialog closes (the modal is kept mounted by the settings page). The blob URL created in `handleSetup` is only revoked when a new one is created, never on unmount or close, so each setup leaks a blob for the lifetime of the page. Clear both in `resetState()` and revoke the URL (e.g. in a cleanup effect).

findings.title: Clipboard write rejection is unhandled and success toast is shown unconditionally
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs immediately. In contexts where the Clipboard API is unavailable or permission is denied (non-HTTPS deployments, some browsers), the user is told the codes were copied while nothing was copied, and the rejection surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection. Await the call and only show success on resolve, with an error toast/fallback otherwise.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle made unreachable by keyboard
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button removes it from tab order, so keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer toggle password visibility. This change affects every `PasswordField` in the app, not just the 2FA dialogs. If the intent was to keep tab order flowing to the next form field, consider other means (e.g. ordering/`aria` handling) rather than making the control unfocusable.

findings.title: Backup codes are unusable for Google/SAML users with 2FA
findings.body: For users who reach the login page via the external TOTP flow (`totpEmail` set, i.e. Google/SAML accounts with 2FA), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered and the new "Lost access" button is never shown, so those users cannot use their backup codes. Even if a `backupCode` were submitted, `authorize()` in next-auth-options.ts throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` at the `user.identityProvider !== CAL && !credentials.totpCode` check before reaching the backup-code branch. These users have no recovery path if they lose their authenticator, which is the main purpose of the feature.
